# Executive Summary: Q1 2026 Call Forecast and Staffing

**For:** Director of Customer Care (simulated regional home-internet provider)
**Data:** synthetic, generated by `src/generate_data.py` (seed 42). All figures describe a simulated contact center.

## Decisions requested

1. **Hire 4 agents now.** The roster of 48 FTE falls short in 12 of 12 weeks in Q1. Training takes 6 weeks, so new agents are productive from 2026-02-12 at the earliest.
2. **Approve $16,811 of overtime for Q1** to cover the gap until the new hires are ready. This includes $4,028 for the February 2 price-change notice.

## What the forecast says

| | Q1 2026 |
|---|---|
| Calls expected (baseline) | 64,415 (7.3% more than Q1 2025) |
| Extra calls from the Feb 2 notice | about 530, mostly Feb 2-6 |
| Average agents needed (FTE) | 50.3 vs. 48 on the roster |
| Peak week | 54.0 FTE, week of 2026-02-02 |

- **How much to trust it.** We tested the method by forecasting 13 weeks ahead from 8 past starting points. It missed by 3.4% on average, compared with 7.7% for "same as last week." The stated 80% ranges captured 80% of actual days.
- **The notice effect is measured, not assumed.** The September 2025 notice raised billing and cancellation calls 35% on the day it went out. The extra volume halved about every 2.6 days, and calls ran 8.1% longer for two weeks.

## Why act now

The center answered 73.4% of calls within 60 seconds in 2025, against a goal of 80%, and 10.2% of callers hung up. Volume grows about 0.62% a month, and the schedule has not kept pace.

## Worth exploring

Five separate queues each need their own buffer of idle agents. If one cross-trained team answered every queue, the same service level would need about 20 fewer FTE. A pilot cross-training billing and cancellations would test how much of that saving holds in practice.
